summary_out.outcome: pnl 4454.50 (+490.98% vs vol-regime-sizer base 753.75; -5.04% vs lineage parent g3l2 4690.75 — REGRESSION inside the pre-declared >2% regression band; -5.84% from the g3l2 PnL high), sharpe 19.66 (+0.554 vs g3l2; essentially flat), max_dd -0.39% (unchanged from g3l2 -0.40%), win_rate 0.3833 (-0.57pp vs g3l2 0.3890), trade_count 80,072 (+6.60% vs g3l2 75,115; loosening admitted 4957 additional orders), is_weighted_bps 0.0550 (-5.89% vs g3l2 0.0585 — the predicted bps narrowing did materialize on surviving orders, but did not translate into PnL because the [1.5, 2.0] band trades carry net-negative EV). Hypothesis option (a) FALSIFIED: 1.5 was on or near the size-asym EV peak, not over-restrictive as the gen-3 migration's base_specific (3) reading suggested.
summary_out.hypothesis: vrs's chop+spread two-gate base has substantial headroom (per the gen-3 migration base_specific (3) finding), and the 1.5 size-asymmetry threshold was ported from a four-gate composition with less headroom — so the marginal gate fires harder on vrs and 1.5 is likely over-restrictive here. Loosening to 2.0 (top of the recommended [1.25, 2.0] band) should give back trade count and bps quality while preserving most of the PnL gain, because [1.5, 2.0]-band trades sit closer to the body of the depth-asymmetry distribution than to the tail.
summary_out.next: Two strong primary candidates for g4l2 on island-2, in priority order. (a) PRIMARY: tighten size_asym_ratio to 1.25 — the OPPOSITE direction from g4l1. The regression at 2.0 combined with the bps-narrowing-without-PnL-gain pattern indicates 1.5 sits near the EV peak; the more informative falsification is now on the tight flank. A regression at 1.25 confirms 1.5 is a peak; a confirmation at 1.25 reveals the peak is actually tighter and g3l2 itself was loose. Either outcome maps the local EV curvature with the highest information per loop. (b) SECONDARY: add a 4th orthogonal axis with a CALIBRATED-not-ported threshold — specifically a flow gate with a stricter threshold than g3l1's 6/4s (which failed on vrs); recommended z >= 9 or 10 imbalance over 4s. The gen-3 migration's generalizable (2) noted weak-threshold flow gates tend to fail, but a high-z flow threshold is structurally distant from chop/spread/size-asym and remains untested on vrs. Island-1 g4l1 just demonstrated that adding orthogonal axes on top of heavy stacks tends to inert at thresholds ported from other islands (null result on velocity), so any 4th-axis attempt needs a calibrated rather than ported threshold. AVOID: 1.75 (the migration-suggested next-after-regression value) — it bisects [1.5, 2.0] and likely produces a noisy near-null with low information; tightening to 1.25 gives a wider sweep of the ratio axis with the same number of loops. DO: surface co-skip counters from g4l1 stdout for the bps-vs-PnL diagnostic — if size-asym is firing alone (not stacked with chop/spread), the marginal trades it admits are exactly the high-cost wide-spread / heavy-chop slice that the other two gates would have caught anyway, which would explain why loosening is net negative.
